args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18 across us-east, us-west, and eu-west). I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all three production regions. Post-rollback status: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production and v2.3.1-rc is unhealthy in staging; neither should be redeployed until the failure is root-caused. Follow-up needed: investigate the v2.3.1 failure and confirm the rollback in the regions.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Why v2.3.0:** It's the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production, and v2.3.1-rc is unhealthy in staging only.
- **Result:** All regions are now on v2.3.0. The service reports healthy, with the error rate down from 0.18 to 0.002.
- **Approval:** None needed, since v2.3.0 has a healthy production history.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback, and the post-rollback status. It also says v2.3.1 and v2.3.1-rc shouldn't be redeployed until the failure is root-caused.

content.text: I'll start by pulling the release history and current status for checkout-api.

The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production, and v2.3.1-rc is only in staging. Since v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, rolling back to it doesn't need change-manager approval. I'll roll back now.
The rollback succeeded. I'll confirm service health before opening the incident.
